clue.text: Bodice needs adjusting containing one's unruliness

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the extra piece somewhere within them
adjusting the bodice's fit stands for reworking these letters into a new order

parts.note: one's is read as one is; one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's bodice must be altered to rein in some unruly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusting' rearranges BODICE NEEDS; 'containing' puts I among those letters; the 's is just 'is' joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey rules or orders is unruly behaviour, a close synonym.

clue.text: Detectives run around bend

parts.note: DIS is the plural of DI, detective inspector

indicators.note: around turns the word for run back to front

parts.note: to trot is to run at a jog

explanation.surface: Police officers jog round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bend' looks like the corner the officers run round, but it is the definition, a verb meaning to warp.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend something out of its proper shape, physically or in meaning, is to twist or warp it.

clue.text: Small painting's start holding small brush

indicators.note: the outer pair of letters hold the little word between them

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A tiny painting begins with a small brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts WEE between S and P, the first letter of 'painting's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a long brushing stroke, and to sweep is to brush a floor clean.

clue.text: Ale takes action on English yeoman

indicators.note: takes means the drink swallows the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a feat is a notable action or deed

explanation.surface: Beer prompts an Englishman of the yeoman class to act.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London, so 'English yeoman' fits the surface while only 'yeoman' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeater is the popular name for a Yeoman Warder of the Tower of London, so an example of a yeoman.

clue.text: Ruin atmosphere that's on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the mood of a place is its atmosphere

explanation.surface: A gloomy atmosphere lifting turns out to be ruinous after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's on the up' reverses MOOD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is ruin or destruction as a fate, the end awaiting someone.

clue.text: This could signify a lift for Trump!

definitions.text: This could signify a lift for Trump!

parts.words: This could signify a lift for Trump!
parts.note: Trump stands for any American, and the American word for a British lift is the definition; the surface suggests a boost in his poll ratings

explanation.surface: Something that might give the President a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lift' in Britain is the machine carrying people between floors; Americans call it by another name, and Trump here is just a typical American speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this word for the cabin that carries people between storeys, which Britons call a lift.

clue.text: Caught past fielding position

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
over can mean past, finished

explanation.surface: A cricket catch taken by a fielder who once stood in some position.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position on the off side in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, cover is a named off-side position where a fielder stands.

clue.text: Put tackle in hot water

indicators.note: in places the gear inside the angry word

parts.note: hot under the collar means irate, angry
rig and tackle both mean gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Someone drops their fishing tackle into hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hot water' looks like a phrase meaning trouble, but 'water' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water through channels or sprinklers.

clue.text: Premier accepts explosive command

indicators.note: accepts means the first word takes the short piece inside itself

parts.note: premier means first, the best
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister takes on board an explosive order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' poses as the Prime Minister but means best.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at someone's behest means doing it at their order or bidding.

clue.text: Docker night and day inside hold

indicators.note: inside puts the evening-and-day pair within the word for hold

parts.note: to store something is to hold it
eve means the evening, the night before

explanation.surface: A dock worker labours night and day down in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like the ship's cargo space, apt for a docker, but here it means store.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a worker who loads and unloads ships, a docker.

clue.text: Lover sensitively penning poetry

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the answer is held within these two words

explanation.surface: A tender lover writes poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, fitting the poetry, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing, the same thing as poetry.

clue.text: Very large quarry for predatory bird

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, clothing for very large people
the quarry of a hunter is its prey

explanation.surface: A huge victim is targeted by a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label meaning very large.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk, a bird that hunts its food.

clue.text: Fine hose put on thigh lastly

indicators.note: put on means the hose goes after that letter
lastly means take only the closing letter of the word

parts.note: an airline is a hose that delivers compressed air

explanation.surface: Fine stockings drawn up the thigh to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' looks like stockings but is an air hose; 'Fine' is an adjective, as in a very narrow crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is extremely thin, as narrow as a single hair.

clue.text: Fruit also saves mother time

indicators.note: saves means keeps the other pieces safely inside

parts.note: too means also
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Fruit also spares Mum some time in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, though cooked as a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is botanically a fruit, the seed-bearing body of its plant.

clue.text: Thrash metal duo soften

indicators.note: to thrash something is to beat it about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrash-metal duo tones down their sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrash metal' reads as a music genre, but 'Thrash' is the instruction to rearrange METAL DUO.
explanation.definitionFit: To modulate a voice or sound is to adjust or tone it down, to soften it.

clue.text: Prophecy about to be found in wood

indicators.note: to be found in places the short word inside the woodland word

parts.note: a forest is a large wood
CA, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A seer's prediction is about to be found deep in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, Latin for about, used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction of what will happen, a kind of prophecy.

clue.text: One's plan adequately describes walk

indicators.note: describes in its old sense of encircling: the phrase goes round the answer

explanation.surface: Someone's plan sets out a walk well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means draws around, as a compass describes a circle, so the answer sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, usually by the sea, laid out for walking.

clue.text: Steep charge supporting staff

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A high fee is charged to back the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for the charge but is a verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate food is to soften it by soaking in liquid, which is to steep it.

clue.text: Team facing Spanish team of stars

parts.note: a side is a sports team
Real Madrid, the Spanish football club, is often shortened to Real

explanation.surface: A side lining up against a Spanish club full of star players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of stars' looks like praise for the football team but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective for things relating to the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: Underground deviation with transport going north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the pair is written upwards

parts.note: yaw is a ship's or aircraft's deviation from its course
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A detour on the Underground, with trains heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' reverses YAW plus BUS together to give the North American word for an underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the subway is the underground railway, what Londoners call the Tube.

clue.text: Most fit old man's upset before examination

indicators.note: before puts the reversed piece ahead of the exam
upset means turned over, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for one's father, the old man
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Dad is upset ahead of a fitness check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses PA to AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable, so the superlative is the most suitable or fitting.

clue.text: Crowds seeing run in revealing underwear

indicators.note: in puts the single letter within the underwear word

parts.note: thongs are skimpy, revealing knickers
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Crowds gawp at a jogger in skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Throngs are dense crowds of people, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Pillar of America consumed by boasting

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the boasting word

parts.note: bluster is loud, boastful talk

explanation.surface: A pillar of American society eaten up by his own bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pillar of America' reads like a phrase, but 'Pillar' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short pillars supporting a handrail or balustrade.

clue.text: Minister to split moving right to centre

indicators.note: moving signals that one letter of the split word changes place
to centre says where the moved letter goes: the middle of the word

parts.note: to sever is to split or cut apart

explanation.surface: A minister breaks with his party by shifting to the centre ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving right to centre' sounds political, but R shifts from the end of SEVER to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to attend to or serve their needs.

clue.text: Harry is naughty then good with Queen

parts.note: bad means naughty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Prince Harry was a bad boy, then reformed with the Queen's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' poses as the prince but is a verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester or harass them persistently, as is to badger.

clue.text: Show man's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is said and heard

parts.note: man's read as a guy's, a guy being a man

explanation.surface: A man's TV show goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' is a noun meaning outward appearance, not a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or pretence, a show put on.

clue.text: Attack anyway, taking on Stoke's centre

indicators.note: taking on means the word absorbs another piece

parts.note: but, at the start of a remark, works like anyway or however

indicators.note: the centre is the middle letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: Launching an attack regardless, a team takes on Stoke's central defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke is Stoke City, an English football club; its centre is O. 'Attack' here is a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a spell or attack, as in a bout of flu.

clue.text: One initially acquires competence taking on roles

definitions.text: One initially acquires competence taking on roles

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A novice gradually learns the trade by taking parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a performer gains skill by playing parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer learns the craft by playing parts on stage or screen.

clue.text: Trouble with part for love

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a ration is a portion or allotted part

explanation.surface: Trouble with an acting role in a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a theatrical role but is a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship of someone.

clue.text: Without adult moulded earthen vessel anyhow

indicators.note: moulded, as clay is shaped, means the remaining letters are reformed
without means the adult letter is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A potter's earthen pot was shaped without any grown-up's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes A from EARTHEN VESSEL; 'moulded' rearranges the twelve letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless and anyhow both mean in spite of that, all the same.
